clue.text: Husband and wife in tune on piano

blocks.note: p is the musical marking for piano, softly
an air is a melody

explanation.surface: A married couple playing a melody together at the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' puts the tune after the piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A married couple is a twosome, a matched set of two people.

clue.text: An expression, in other words

blocks.note: surface reading: 'in other words' looks like a throwaway phrase meaning 'that is to say'
setter's reading: a restatement of something using different wording

explanation.walkthrough: 'In other words' looks like a filler phrase, but it is the literal description of the answer: a saying put into other wording.
explanation.definitionFit: A restatement of a text or saying in different language is exactly an expression rendered in other words.

clue.text: Country home raised help

indicators.note: in a down clue something raised is read from the bottom upwards, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: being in means being at home
aid is assistance

explanation.surface: A rural house that has been built with assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the South Asian nation, a large republic and so a country.

clue.text: She may drive you round the bend!

definitions.text: She may drive you round the bend!

blocks.note: surface reading: an idiom meaning to make you lose your mind with irritation
setter's reading: a woman employed to drive you in a car, steering round corners in the road

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for exasperating someone is taken literally: a female employee driving a car round a bend.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived word names a woman whose job is driving a private car for an employer.

clue.text: Bound to put an end to game

blocks.note: to hop is to bound or leap
to scotch a rumour or plan is to stop it

explanation.surface: Someone obliged to stop a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' reads as 'obliged', but it is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: The playground pastime of jumping through chalked squares is a children's game.

clue.text: One in Paris lit up before

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading the word from the bottom, backwards

blocks.note: un is French for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone in Paris lighting up earlier, perhaps a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Both work as conjunctions of time: wait until dawn means wait up to the moment before dawn ends.

clue.text: Game? Worldly female shot bags duck

indicators.note: something shot is ruined or wrecked, so the letters are scattered into a new order
to bag is to put into a sack, so one part holds the other inside

blocks.note: taken as written
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, zero

explanation.surface: A sophisticated woman hunting game shoots a duck and bags it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' and 'shot' and 'duck' all suggest hunting; the question mark marks the answer as one particular game.
explanation.definitionFit: The children's pastime in which everyone copies the moves of whoever is in front is a game.

clue.text: Not paid for by someone else, so no medical care given

definitions.text: Not paid for by someone else

blocks.clueFragment: Not paid for by someone else
blocks.note: first meaning: nobody stood you a drink or meal
second meaning: a patient or wound left without therapy

explanation.walkthrough: The word splits as 'un-treated', not bought a treat, and also means lacking treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Being treated means having something bought for you or receiving therapy; the negative covers both senses.

clue.text: Girl employed by United Nations

indicators.note: what is employed by a body sits inside it, so the letters are found within the phrase

blocks.note: the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A young woman working for the UN.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female given name, and crosswords use 'girl' for any such name.

clue.text: A good opener should have a good one

definitions.text: A good opener should have a good one

blocks.note: surface reading: something that opens well, like a tin opener or an opening line
setter's reading: an opening batsman in cricket should score many runs per innings over a season

explanation.walkthrough: An opener in cricket is a batsman who goes in first; his worth is judged by his runs per completed innings.
explanation.definitionFit: The statistic is a cricketer's total runs divided by the number of times out, the measure of a batsman.

clue.text: North Coast resort, favourite for VIP treatment?

blocks.note: Redcar is a seaside town on the north-east coast of England
a teacher's pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A seaside town tipped as the top destination for celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: A crimson strip laid out for dignitaries stands for lavish welcome given to important guests, by metonymy.

clue.text: Divulge information got from head of Lancing College

indicators.note: the head of a word is its very front, so only its opening letter is used

blocks.note: the first letter of Lancing
Eton is the famous English public school, Eton College

explanation.surface: A secret leaked by the headmaster of Lancing, an English boarding school.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancing College is a real school, so the phrase looks like one title; it splits into a letter and a different college.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal a secret is the phrasal verb meaning to disclose or admit what you know.

clue.text: Suitable card for one who plays tricks

blocks.note: practical means suitable for use
the joker is a playing card

explanation.surface: Choosing the right card to play in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card' can also mean a funny person, which suits the definition, but here it is the playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: A prankster who sets up physical pranks on people is known by this name.

clue.text: St Peter, he worried about name, name given to Satan

indicators.note: worried means shaken and tugged about, so the letters are scrambled
about means surrounding, so the scrambled letters go round the other part

blocks.note: taken as written
n is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: The saint at heaven's gate fretting over what to call the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the tempter in Eden is a snake, and that title became an epithet for the devil.

clue.text: Mature Rhode Island writer

blocks.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for the US state
a pen is something that writes

explanation.surface: A seasoned author from the smallest US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mature' looks like an adjective for the writer; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs both mean to grow ready or developed, as fruit does over time.

clue.text: Pale sun in . . surprisingly . . Iberia?

indicators.note: what happens surprisingly comes out unexpectedly, so the letters land in an unexpected order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A weak sun is a surprise in sunny Spain and Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows Iberia is an example: Spain and Portugal sit on land almost surrounded by sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberia is the landmass joined to Europe on one side and bounded by water elsewhere, an instance of the answer.

clue.text: Try to correspond with international

blocks.note: to test is to try out
things that match correspond

explanation.surface: An instruction to try writing to someone abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'International' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun for a game between national sides, as in cricket or rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: A full-length cricket or rugby game between two countries is called an international.

clue.text: Deal with the enemy? That may cause one to undergo a term of imprisonment

blocks.note: to serve a customer is to deal with them
'time, the enemy' is a proverbial phrase for time's hostility to us

explanation.surface: Collaborating with the enemy would land a traitor in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Dealing with the enemy reads as treason, which fits the prison idea, but the enemy here is time.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend a sentence behind bars is the idiom for completing a jail term.

clue.text: One trying to get brown bear, hunts camouflaged?

indicators.note: something camouflaged is disguised, so the letters appear in a changed form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hunter in disguise trying to shoot a brown bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown bear' reads as the animal; 'brown' belongs to the definition and means tanned.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lying out in sunshine to tan is trying to make their skin go brown.

clue.text: Cover very large bathing beaches

blocks.note: a lid is a cover
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: Huge seaside resorts being shielded.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian-derived word means a public swimming place or beach resort.

clue.text: For sale by auction, three European articles (bone)

blocks.note: French un, German der and English the are each an article
the hammer, or malleus, is a small bone of the middle ear

explanation.surface: An auction lot of three Continental items made of bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' suggests lots in a sale, but these are the grammar words 'a' and 'the' in three languages.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods up for bids are said to go under the auctioneer's gavel, the idiom used here.

clue.text: Ton, approximately, in trunk

blocks.note: t is the abbreviation for ton
'or so' means approximately, as in ten or so

explanation.surface: About a ton of luggage packed in a travelling chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' suggests luggage; it is the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the human body is the part without head and limbs.

clue.text: I am to be found in Michigan tourist centre

indicators.note: being found in something means sitting inside it, so one part goes within the other

blocks.note: MI is the postal abbreviation for the state
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone saying they live in a Michigan holiday town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florida city is famous for beaches and draws huge numbers of holidaymakers.

clue.text: Goddess, in emergency, letting crown slip

indicators.note: letting something slip means losing it, so the abbreviation for crown is dropped

blocks.note: a crisis is an emergency
CR is the abbreviation for crown

explanation.surface: A deity in a crisis whose headgear falls off.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief Egyptian mother deity was worshipped as a goddess across the ancient world.

clue.text: Article on very good American composer

blocks.note: so means very, as in 'so good'
US is short for United States, American
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about a fine American musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the article after the rest. 'Very good' stands for so, a loose stretch of 'so' meaning very.
explanation.definitionFit: John Philip Sousa wrote marches such as The Stars and Stripes Forever, so he was a composer.

clue.text: Treat Eire, reconstituted, as state again

indicators.note: reconstituted means put together again in another form, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Dealing with Ireland, once restructured, as a nation once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a noun for a nation, which suits Eire; it is the verb, to say.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeat something said before is to say it a second time.

clue.text: What an architect may have built, some called weird

definitions.text: What an architect may have built

indicators.note: weird means strange and out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An architect's building that some people called bizarre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Built' suggests a full-size building; architects also make miniatures of their designs.
explanation.definitionFit: A miniature replica in exact proportion is the kind of thing architects construct to show a design.

clue.text: Vast sum of money in strongroom in treasury

blocks.note: first meaning: a fortune, as in costing a packet
second meaning: the place where a state's coins are struck

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses concern money: an informal word for a fortune, and the establishment that produces coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a fortune is called this, and it also names the official works that manufacture coins for the treasury.
